options.name: commands
options.description: The commands allowed by the sudoers rule. Multiple can be added by passing a list of commands. Use V(ALL) for all commands.

options.name: defaults
options.description: A list of C(Defaults) directives to include in the sudoers rule file. Each entry is written as a C(Defaults) line scoped to the user or group specified in the rule. For example, V(!targetpw) becomes C(Defaults:%group !targetpw) for a group rule or C(Defaults:user !targetpw) for a user rule. The directives are placed before the privilege rule in the generated file.

options.name: group
options.description: The name of the group for the sudoers rule. This option cannot be used in conjunction with O(user).

options.name: host
options.description: Specify the host the rule is for.

options.name: name
options.description: The name of the sudoers rule. This is used for the filename for the sudoers file managed by this rule.

options.name: noexec
options.description: Whether a command is prevented to run further commands itself.

options.name: nopassword
options.description: Whether a password is not required when command is run with sudo.

options.name: runas
options.description: Specify the target user the command(s) runs as.

options.name: setenv
options.description: Whether to allow keeping the environment when command is run with sudo.

options.name: state
options.description: Whether the rule should exist or not.

options.name: sudoers_path
options.description: The path which sudoers config files are managed in.

options.name: user
options.description: The name of the user for the sudoers rule. This option cannot be used in conjunction with O(group).

options.name: validation
options.description: If V(absent), the sudoers rule is added without validation. If V(detect) and C(visudo) is available, then the sudoers rule is validated by C(visudo). If V(required), C(visudo) must be available to validate the sudoers rule.
